correctness.rationale: A simplicial distribution support admits the integral facet matrix A (Kharoof–Lai Proposition 3.16), with affine carrier dimension equal to its real kernel dimension minus one. On a closed manifold the orientation local system supplies compatible local facet orientations; for each lifted codimension-one face, its two possible base-side incidences have opposite signs. Thus the top local-coefficient normalized boundary is the same integer matrix up to unimodular diagonal sign changes. The supported complex has no cells above dimension n, so its top twisted homology is precisely the kernel, whose rank equals real nullity. Pullback orientation-cover anti-invariants yield the rational formula; connected covering components give the explicit probability simplex. Exact RP2 matrices verify ordinary rank 10, twisted rank 9, five disjoint-copy cases.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating work gives a homology-based carrier criterion only for orientable bases. Identifying the correct orientation-twisted top homology removes this structural limitation on every closed manifold, restores a genuine intrinsic topological invariant, and gives a double-cover computational interpretation. Exact projective-plane examples show that ordinary integral top homology can vanish while carrier dimensions vary arbitrarily, whereas the twisted formula remains exact. The covering corollary classifies whole probability polytopes with component degrees and nondeterministic vertices; the fact is not merely another small numerical enumeration. Existing facet matrices already compute dimensions algebraically, acknowledged as a limitation rather than omitted.
